source.title: Evidence for feature-specific error correction in LLMs
source.citation: Francisco Ferreira da Silva et al., 2026
source.authors: Francisco Ferreira da Silva; S. Heimersheim

record.tranche_reason: Tests an empirical prediction associated with computation in superposition using activation-perturbation response geometry, rather than measuring individual-neuron polysemanticity directly.
record.gate_note: The study measures whether candidate feature directions are more privileged than mixtures under residual-stream perturbations. It does not test whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs or how often neurons are polysemantic. The steering examples and cited results are not separate measurements of the claim.
record.test_reason: The study tests feature-specific error correction: whether residual-stream candidate feature directions are more perturbation-sensitive than their mixtures (superellipse exponent p > 2). It never measures individual neurons, whether they respond to unrelated inputs, or how often they are polysemantic. Superposition is assumed as motivation, and the toy model is built to operate in superposition. A p > 2 result for residual-stream directions is a related but different construct from neuron polysemanticity or its cause, so V3 is not tested. The finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that candidate feature directions (contrastive, MELBO, SAE) are privileged, with p > 2 against p ≈ 2 for controls, replicated across six models and many settings. They present this as consistent with superposition and error correction, call p ≈ 2.3 likely a lower bound, and note alternative explanations: learned robustness, or a manifold mechanism. They also state that p > 2 is necessary but not sufficient for a direction to be a feature.
record.recipe_differences: Uses residual-stream activation perturbations and fits superellipse exponents to downstream response; it does not inspect individual-neuron image responses or use a neuron-level polysemanticity measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported contrastive-direction p values remain above 2 across tested perturbation and measurement layers, response metrics, threshold levels, perturbation methods, activation sources, token positions, and models. Rotating directions away from contrastive candidates lowers p toward 2.

fits_no_version.finding: Candidate feature directions in the residual stream have p > 2: contrastive mean 2.42, MELBO 2.21, SAE 2.28. Controls sit near 2: PCA 2.03, random-difference 2.05, random 2.03. Contrastive results hold across six LLMs and ablations (means 2.24–2.63). p falls toward 2 when directions are rotated away from the candidates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLMs show feature-specific error correction: residual-stream feature directions are privileged over their mixtures under perturbation, as computation in superposition predicts.

fits_no_version.finding: A two-layer denoising toy model built to compute in superposition gives p of 3–3.4 on ground-truth feature directions. p rises with the feature-to-neuron ratio and falls toward 2 as directions are rotated away from the true features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks computing in superposition privilege feature directions, giving superellipse exponent p > 2.

record.problems: The LLM experiments use candidate feature directions rather than ground-truth features and do not measure neuron polysemanticity directly. The authors note that activation plateaus may reflect learned robustness or movement back toward a lower-dimensional manifold rather than error correction. The toy model differs substantially from LLMs in depth, feature type, and activation function.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows omitted. The paper's per-direction and per-setting figure distributions are summarized only where the text provides aggregate values or explicit trends; individual plotted values are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: Image-classifier neurons responding to unrelated inputs.
Share and layer distribution of polysemantic MLP neurons in LMs.
Whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by packing more sparse features than neurons. The study only tests direction privilege under perturbation, assuming superposition.
Dependence on activation function, architecture or regularization, and the performance cost of reducing it.
Dependence of polysemanticity on the activation range examined or the scoring method.

record.verdict_notes: No neuron-level analysis appears anywhere in the paper, so the reader's V3 'tests' link and its supports labels are removed. Superposition is taken as a premise, and the work concerns residual-stream directions, not polysemantic neurons. The SAE result is for Gemma-2-9B only.

versions.untested_parts: Image-classifier neurons and their responses to unrelated image inputs.
Polysemantic MLP neurons in language models, unrelated tokens or contexts, and layerwise prevalence.

The study tests feature-specific error correction as a prediction associated with computation in superposition, but does not count polysemantic neurons, establish that LLMs represent more sparse features than dimensions, or directly establish that superposition causes neuron-level mixed selectivity.
Polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Changes in the share of polysemantic neurons across activation functions, architectures, or regularization, and performance costs of reducing that share.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons have coherent shared features or whether truly unrelated mixtures are rare.
Whether neuron polysemanticity depends on activation-range selection or explanation-scoring methods.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B
rows.operation_detail: Fit superellipse exponent p to plateau-breaking angles for mixtures of contrastive directions.
rows.uncertainty: 95% CI [2.29, 2.62] on the mean, direction bootstrap
rows.note: Authors interpret p > 2 as candidate feature directions being more sensitive than their mixtures; it is indirect evidence for an implication of computation in superposition, not a neuron-polysemanticity measurement.
rows.check: Measures direction privilege (p) for contrastive residual-stream directions, not neuron polysemanticity or its cause; cannot bear on V3 as stated.

rows.subject: Two-layer denoising toy model (Vaintrob, 2026)
rows.operation_detail: Fit superellipse exponent p to perturbations aligned with ground-truth feature axes and to rotated directions.

conditions.value: Directions rotated away from true features toward random directions

rows.value: p in the range 3–3.4 for ground-truth feature directions; degrades monotonically toward 2 as directions rotate away
rows.uncertainty: Interquartile range shown in Figure 7; numerical bounds not stated
rows.note: The authors describe this as validation in a toy model and caution against placing much weight on its specific values because its architecture and activation differ substantially from LLMs.
rows.check: Toy model is constructed to compute in superposition, with a fixed random encoder and no gradient training. It validates the method and does not show that superposition causes polysemantic neurons.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Candidate feature directions in Gemma-2-9B, with the reported cross-model and setup ablations
reader_labels.reason: Contrastive, MELBO, and SAE candidate directions have p > 2 while PCA and random controls are approximately p = 2 (R1-R7); rotation away from contrastive directions reduces p toward 2 (R8). This supports the authors' proposed FSEC prediction of computation in superposition, but is indirect evidence and does not establish neuron-level polysemanticity or its cause.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Toy denoising network with known feature directions and more features than neurons
reader_labels.reason: The toy network gives p in the range 3–3.4 on true feature directions, moving toward 2 as directions rotate away (R9), consistent with the proposed feature-privileging prediction in that toy setting.
